notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix; it is the defect this pass records on 1985-GR-VI.5.9.5-6. §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR6 restricts a numeric edited string to 'certain combinations' of its symbols, where 'The allowable combinations are determined from the order of precedence of symbols and the editing rules', and requires that 'The number of digit positions that can be represented in the PICTURE character-string must range from 1 to 18 inclusive' and that 'The character-string must contain at least one' editing symbol. Implemented at 85: AnalyzeCharacterString makes a string with an editing symbol (or a 9-string under BLANK WHEN ZERO) NumericEdited and counts 9, Z, *, every P and each floating occurrence after the first as DigitPositions; ScreenPictureDigitCapacity and CheckDigitCapacity hold that count to 1 through EditionInfo.MaxDigits (18 below 2002): PIC Z(18), $(19) and +(19) compile, PIC Z(19), Z(18)P, $(20), +(20) and *(18).99 get COBOL0802, PIC $, + and B get COBOL1934; S beside an editing symbol, and A or X beside any but B 0 /, are refused by the precedence walk. Not implemented at 85: PictureComposition.Precedence walks the 2023 Table 10 at every edition. The 1985 chart is cell for cell that table (compared by script, all 441 cells) except that it has one non-floating cs row and column, and Precedence also offers a fixed currency symbol the 2023 trailing role (PicRole.CurrencyTrailing, §2023:13.18.40.3 SR26, first allowed by §2002:13.16.38.2 SR23), so PIC 999$, +999$ and 999$CR define numeric edited items at --std 85. The witness is the refusal of PIC Z(18)9.

next.reason: 1985: numeric edited uses 'B', '/', 'P', 'V', 'Z', '0', '9', ',', '.', '*', '+', '-', 'CR', 'DB', cs; 'The number of digit positions ... must range from 1 to 18 inclusive'; at least one editing symbol. §2023:13.18.40.4 GR13 a) defines fixed-point numeric-edited by an equivalent symbol test, combinations per §2023:13.18.40.3 SR2, content per §2023:13.18.40.4 GR14, but §2023:13.18.40.3 SR14 allows 'from 1 through 31' digit positions for fixed-point numeric-edited items: 19 to 31 digit edited pictures refused in 1985 are accepted. Floating-point edited items (GR13 b) are new.
